text:
Talia Benson: Dogfood triage time. I pulled notes from the roundup doc + the last 2 days of folks running templates. Goal: pick top 10 papercuts for a patch release, assign owners, and decide what we punt.

Talia Benson: Please reply in-thread with (a) what you hit, (b) severity (blocks vs annoying), (c) any quick fix idea.

Renee Sullivan: Ran `rag-python-fastapi` from scratch on a clean laptop. Biggest block: README says `REDWOOD_API_KEY` but the app reads `REDWOOD_API_TOKEN` (or vice versa). I ended up grepping the repo. Severity: BLOCKS.

Dana Lo: +1. Same in TS agent template too. Also our env var docs mention `REDWOOD_BASE_URL` but code expects `REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL`. Severity: BLOCKS.

Sabrina James: Agent template: tool calling example fails if you run behind a corp proxy because streaming drops ~30-60s in. It’s not obvious that we should set keepalive / proxy buffering off + use the SDK helper reconnect pattern. Severity: BLOCKS for some.

Monica Patel: On streaming disconnects: SDK helper in python is fine but the template’s usage is slightly off (we don’t retry on `ECONNRESET` in TS example). Also our default read timeout is too low for ingest + first token on cold start. Severity: BLOCKS for larger docs / slower networks.

Ibrahim Khan: Another one: retries/backoff. Template currently retries 429 the same as 500 (no jitter, no cap). We should align with SDK recommendations: respect `Retry-After`, exponential + jitter, and stop retrying on 4xx except 408/409/429. Severity: annoying but also support ticket driver.

Wei Chen: Docs drift: quickstart page snippet still shows `docker compose up rag` but compose service name is `rag-app`. I got a “no such service” error. Severity: ANNOYING but very visible.

Elliot Price: + docs drift in 2 places (landing page and per-template README). Also the “Production checklist” links to a non-existent section anchor. I can fix the docs but we should also add the snippet extraction check to catch this.

Sean Gallagher: SRE angle: default logging is way too noisy at INFO (every chunk of streamed tokens logged). Also missing request_id in a couple log lines so Console correlation is broken when you’re grepping. Severity: ANNOYING -> quickly becomes painful.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Also our “default dashboards” alert rules are a little aggressive in the pack (p95 latency alert fires on first run). For quickstarts, we should have alerts off by default or use burn-rate style w/ longer windows.

Nadia Rahman: Cost attribution: token usage shows up in Console for hosted calls, but template isn’t tagging `tenant` / `route` consistently so dashboards are empty unless you guess filters. Code has `tenant_id` but telemetry contract says `tenant`. Severity: ANNOYING but makes the “observable by default” claim look fake.

Logan Wright: Telemetry contract mismatch is real: trace attrs use `redwood.request_id` in python but `request.id` in TS. We should standardize in the shared lib + add a validation on startup that prints missing attrs once.

Marcus Lin: Security papercuts: we should stop recommending putting API keys in `.env` without a big note about `.env` being local-only and gitignored (and we should ship `.env.example` only). Also saw a log line that prints full request headers (includes `Authorization` if proxy forwards). Severity: BLOCKS for enterprise reviewers.

Sahana Iyer: CI: smoke tests are flaky when the vector DB container takes longer to become healthy. Compose healthcheck is there, but the test harness doesn’t wait on it consistently. Severity: ANNOYING (for us) but creates churn.

Connor O'Brien: Release/process: we need a single patch train issue list. If we decide top 10, I’ll cut a patch release branch + tag once merged.

Sergio Costa: Observability pack: import instructions assume Grafana Cloud API key env var `GRAFANA_TOKEN`, but README says `GRAFANA_API_KEY`. Similar env var mismatch situation. Severity: ANNOYING.

Talia Benson: Great, thanks. I’m going to propose top 10 based on “blocks first success” + “support ticket drivers”. Please react with :thumbsup: if you agree, :warning: if you think it shouldn’t be top 10.

Talia Benson: Proposed TOP 10 papercuts (v0.3.x patch):
1) Env var naming inconsistency across templates (`REDWOOD_API_KEY`/`TOKEN`, base URL, org/project) + README mismatch (blocks)
2) Streaming disconnects / proxy behavior guidance + SDK helper usage (blocks for some)
3) Retry/backoff policy for 429 + timeouts defaults too aggressive for ingest (blocks/support)
4) Tool calling safety wrappers: default allow-list + tool timeout wrapper not applied everywhere (security/support)
5) Telemetry contract mismatch: trace attrs + log fields + tenant/route tags inconsistent (observability)
6) Noisy logs / missing request_id correlation on some lines (ops)
7) Docker compose service name mismatch in docs/snippets + snippet drift (onboarding)
8) Vector DB healthcheck wait -> CI flake + occasional local “it’s broken” perception (quality)
9) Secrets guidance: `.env` wording + accidental header logging (security)
10) Observability pack env var mismatch + default alerts too noisy (post-run experience)

Renee Sullivan: :thumbsup: for 1,2,7. Those were my first 15 minutes pain.

Dana Lo: :thumbsup: across. For 2, we should add a note about disabling proxy buffering and Node fetch keepalive.

Monica Patel: :thumbsup: on 3. Default timeouts should be different for (a) ingest worker, (b) interactive chat/agent.

Ibrahim Khan: :thumbsup: on 3. Also add “don’t retry streaming mid-response except reconnect pattern” note.

Wei Chen: :thumbsup: on 7. I can fix docs but I want a guardrail so it doesn’t regress.

Elliot Price: :thumbsup: on 7 + 10. If we stabilize env vars, docs work gets easier.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: on 6 + 10. Please don’t ship alerts that page on first run.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: on 10. Recommend: ship alerts disabled by default; include suggested thresholds in README.

Logan Wright: :thumbsup: on 5. We should not ship v1 if contract differs between py/ts.

Nadia Rahman: :thumbsup: on 5. Tenant/route tags are key for cost panels.

Marcus Lin: :thumbsup: on 9. Also we should scan the examples for accidental header dumps.

Sahana Iyer: :thumbsup: on 8. I can take it.

Talia Benson: Cool. Owners + next actions (please sanity check):

Talia Benson: 1) Env var naming consistency + README alignment
- Owner: Dana Lo (TS) + Sabrina James (Py)
- Support: Wei Chen for docs
- Deliverable: one canonical list + shared config loader enforcing aliases w/ deprecation warnings

Dana Lo: I’ll own overall decision + TS changes. Sabrina, want to split by template?

Sabrina James: Yep, I’ll do python templates + update `.env.example` files.

Talia Benson: 2) Streaming disconnects / proxy guidance + SDK helper usage
- Owner: Monica Patel
- Support: Ibrahim Khan (TS SDK bits) + Elliot Price (docs callout)

Monica Patel: Works. I’ll also add a “known issues: proxies” section + link from template READMEs.

Ibrahim Khan: I can patch the TS sample to use the helper + handle `Retry-After` on reconnect.

Talia Benson: 3) Retry/backoff + timeouts defaults
- Owner: Monica Patel (policy) + Sean Gallagher (SRE sign-off)
- Deliverable: consistent defaults across languages, plus per-route overrides (ingest vs query)

Sean Gallagher: I’ll review the defaults. Request: cap total retry time; and log a single structured warning when we hit 429 backoff.

Talia Benson: 4) Tool calling safety wrappers (allow-list, timeouts, output schema validation)
- Owner: Sabrina James
- Security review: Marcus Lin

Sabrina James: Got it. I’ll audit each tool entrypoint; I think one of the TS examples bypasses the wrapper.

Marcus Lin: Please also ensure tool error messages don’t echo user-provided strings unescaped. I’ll do a quick pass.

Talia Benson: 5) Telemetry contract mismatch (trace/log attrs + tenant/route tags)
- Owner: Logan Wright
- Support: Nadia Rahman (cost tagging expectations)

Logan Wright: I’ll update the shared telemetry helper to emit the contract keys and add a startup validator that prints missing keys once. Need Dana/Sabrina to wire in.

Nadia Rahman: I’ll send exact required dims for Console panels (tenant, route, model, deployment_mode) and cardinality notes.

Talia Benson: 6) Noisy logs + request_id correlation
- Owner: Sean Gallagher
- Support: Dana Lo (TS logging) + Sabrina James (Py logging)

Sean Gallagher: I’ll propose log levels + a “no per-token logs” rule. Also add request_id to every log line via middleware.

Talia Benson: 7) Docs/snippet drift + docker compose service name mismatch
- Owner: Wei Chen
- Support: Elliot Price
- Deliverable: fix docs + add CI check for snippet extraction / compose service references

Wei Chen: Yes. I’ll fix the compose naming references today. Need Sahana to help with CI check if it’s non-trivial.

Sahana Iyer: Sure, loop me in.

Talia Benson: 8) Vector DB healthcheck wait (CI flake + local race)
- Owner: Sahana Iyer
- Support: Connor O'Brien for release gate criteria

Sahana Iyer: I’ll update the smoke harness to wait on compose health + add retry for initial connection.

Connor O'Brien: Add it as a required check for release tags. Flakes were killing us.

Talia Benson: 9) Secrets guidance + accidental header logging
- Owner: Marcus Lin
- Support: Elliot Price (wording) + Sabrina James (code changes)

Marcus Lin: I’ll draft the wording + grep for header dumps. Sabrina, I’ll tag you on any code pointers.

Elliot Price: I’ll update docs to be explicit: `.env` is local-only, never commit, use secret manager in deploy.

Talia Benson: 10) Observability pack env var mismatch + default alerts too noisy
- Owner: Sergio Costa
- Support: Rafael Mendes

Sergio Costa: Yep. I’ll standardize env vars and switch alerts to “examples disabled by default” + doc recommended thresholds.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll send suggested burn-rate style alert configs (2-window) that are less noisy.

Linear: (bot) Talia Benson created tickets: ENG-2861 (env var contract), ENG-2862 (streaming/proxy guidance), ENG-2863 (retry/timeout defaults), ENG-2864 (tool safety audit), ENG-2865 (telemetry contract alignment), ENG-2866 (logging hygiene), ENG-2867 (docs/snippet drift), ENG-2868 (healthcheck wait/CI flake), ENG-2869 (secrets + header logging), ENG-2870 (observability pack alerts/env vars)

Talia Benson: Timeline proposal: patch release by end of next week. Please comment if any of these are >2d effort.

Dana Lo: 1 is doable if we allow aliases temporarily. If we try to hard rename everywhere + docs + SDK at once, it’s a mess. Suggest: accept both, warn on deprecated, and set a removal version.

Monica Patel: 2/3 doable. Biggest unknown is picking timeout defaults that don’t feel random. I’ll propose numbers + rationale and get Sean sign-off.

Sabrina James: 4/9 doable. For 9, I want to double-check we never log `Authorization` even in debug.

Wei Chen: 7 is quick, but the CI snippet check might take longer depending on the docs build pipeline.

Sahana Iyer: 8 is quick-ish. We can add an explicit “wait-for” step in CI and also document `docker compose ps` sanity check.

Logan Wright: 5 might touch both templates and shared libs. If we keep it to mapping keys + validation (not replatforming), it’s fine.

Talia Benson: Decision: we ship aliases + deprecation warnings for env vars; no breaking renames in patch. We’ll do breaking cleanup in the next minor.

Talia Benson: Also: anything NOT in top 10 that we should explicitly punt?

Renee Sullivan: Windows setup was rough (python path issues) but I’d punt. We can add a note later.

Elliot Price: Agree punt Windows. Also punt multi-vector-DB support; keep one backend stable.

Sean Gallagher: Punt tuning batch/cache defaults. That’s “optimize later” territory.

Talia Benson: Cool. I’ll post a summary in #devex after this and link the Linear tickets. Please update ticket status in Linear so we can cut the release cleanly.
